selected_modules.reason: Primary module. The issue summary and explicit ICE location point directly to gcc/fortran/trans-expr.c in alloc_scalar_allocatable_for_assignment, with additional mentioned paths in fortran/trans.c, fortran/trans-decl.c, fortran/parse.c, and fortran/f95-lang.c. The reproducer is entirely gfortran.dg Fortran tests, so the failure most directly belongs to the Fortran frontend/lowering pipeline, especially trans* code that maps resolved Fortran expressions and assignments into GCC trees.

Strong secondary module because one observed ICE is in create_tmp_var at gcc/gimple-expr.c:482. That is shared GIMPLE expression construction infrastructure used by frontend lowering. Since the Fortran trans-expr path appears to trigger malformed or unexpected temporary creation, gimple-expr support may be part of the immediate failure mechanism even if the root cause is in Fortran lowering.

Relevant shared IR module because Fortran trans*.c lowers into generic tree/GIMPLE representations, and crashes in trans-expr or gimple temporary creation often reflect invalid tree construction or misuse of core tree/SSA support. As an intermediate compiler mechanism, tree-core is the closest shared representation layer beneath the Fortran translator.

Plausible supporting module because the failure occurs before optimization passes and during frontend-to-middle-end lowering/expansion boundary. Module docs cover language-independent tree conversion and per-function state machinery used while turning frontend constructs into canonical GCC representations, which is adjacent to Fortran trans.c/trans-expr.c behavior and could participate in bad lowering state.

selected_files.reason: Strongest match and primary surface-trigger file. The issue summary names an ICE in alloc_scalar_allocatable_for_assignment at gcc/fortran/trans-expr.c:10837, and the issue also mentions another trans-expr location at line 11497. Logs additionally show a separate ICE in gfc_conv_variable at gcc/fortran/trans-expr.c:3021 across related reproducers. The file doc says this file translates Fortran expressions and assignments, including allocatable handling, temporaries, descriptors, scalarization fallback, and assignment lowering, which directly fits allocatable-assignment crashes across gfortran.dg tests.

Important translation glue file explicitly mentioned in the issue at lines 1932 and 2332. Its doc describes it as the central lowering driver and shared utility layer that dispatches statement translation and provides temporary/block helpers. Since the observed failures occur before optimization passes and in frontend lowering, trans.cc is a plausible intermediate mechanism or caller context feeding bad state into trans-expr.cc during assignment/expression lowering.

Explicitly referenced by the issue at gcc/fortran/trans-decl.c:6884. Its doc says it builds backend declarations and assembles complete function bodies for gfortran GENERIC translation, including deferred-variable handling and body generation. That makes it a plausible upstream/lowering-context file for allocatable variables and procedure/module entities involved in these compile-time crashes and diagnostics.

Selected as the best remaining explicitly cited upstream file. The issue mentions parse.c at lines 6338 and 6620, and the reproducer set includes compile-only diagnostic cases involving modules and procedure-pointer/type diagnostics (for example 'either an unlimited polymorphic or assumed type' and 'is a procedure pointer'). The doc says parse.cc drives whole-unit parsing, resolution orchestration, and final translation, so it is relevant as the frontend entry/orchestration path that constructs the program units later lowered into the crashing trans-expr assignment code.

Strongest match in this module because the execution log contains a direct ICE at create_tmp_var in gcc/gimple-expr.c:482. Its documented responsibility includes core GIMPLE expression/type predicates, operand validity, and helpers around GIMPLE expression construction/addressability, which fits a Fortran lowering bug that appears to create an invalid or unexpected temporary while translating allocatable assignment expressions.

Also highly relevant because it declares the public temporary-creation and operand-classification APIs used by front ends and lowering code when forming valid GIMPLE operands. Since the observed failures include both create_tmp_var in gimple-expr.c and gfc_conv_variable/alloc_scalar_allocatable_for_assignment in fortran/trans-expr.c, this header is part of the exact frontend-to-GIMPLE contract that may be violated or insufficiently checked.

Plausible intermediate mechanism because it is GCC’s main lowering pass from front-end GENERIC trees into High GIMPLE, including temporary creation and expression lowering. Even though the primary crash site is in Fortran trans-expr.c, the bug concerns malformed lowering before optimization passes, and gimplify is the central shared code that canonicalizes front-end-produced trees into GIMPLE form where bad temporaries or invalid operands can surface.

Relevant companion interface because it exposes the gimplification APIs and helpers for temporary variables, assignment construction, operand predicates, and expression/body lowering. Given the observed boundary between Fortran translation and a shared GIMPLE temporary-creation ICE, this header represents the shared contract likely involved in how the frontend requests or prepares lowered expressions.

Best match within tree-core because it is the core implementation of GCC’s language-independent tree subsystem: constructors, canonicalization, declarations, types, expressions, locations, and generic predicates. The observed failures are before optimization passes and arise while the Fortran frontend lowers code in trans-expr.c, with one alternate ICE in gimple-expr.c:create_tmp_var and another in gfc_conv_variable.
